pwc_ai_fitness.headline: Mining scores lowest of any sector on AI fitness
pwc_ai_fitness.figure: mining had the lowest score of any sector on our AI fitness index... the most AI-fit companies, the study showed, enjoy an AI-driven performance boost that's 7.2 times higher... Indeed, in PwC's 29th Global CEO Survey, 40% of mining CEOs said their company's technology performance was below expectations.
pwc_ai_fitness.title: Mine 2026: Ambition to action
pwc_ai_fitness.scope: Mining-specific, and the 40% is mining chief executives assessing their own technology performance rather than an outside verdict. Printed deliberately: a case that only carries upside reads as a brochure, and this is the figure a sceptical chief executive already has in mind before the meeting starts.

labour_productivity.headline: Output per worker has fallen since 2020
labour_productivity.figure: Output per worker in the mining industry has fallen since 2020... 39% of mining employers expect an inability to attract talent will hinder their transformations.
labour_productivity.title: Mine 2026: Ambition to action
labour_productivity.scope: Industry-wide labour productivity. Used to establish that the gap is a condition of the industry rather than a failing of one operator. Replaces the 2015 MPI decline figure, which McKinsey's own later work restates differently — see `superseded` below.

grade_decline.headline: Head grades down ~40% in three decades
grade_decline.figure: Average copper grades have fallen by roughly 40% since 1991, increasing the value of stable throughput and consistent recovery.
grade_decline.title: 2026 Mining and Metals Industry Outlook
grade_decline.scope: Long-run head grade decline. Names one metal because the publisher does; the point it carries is commodity-neutral — as grade falls, the value of each recovered point rises. This is the reason the recovery argument gets more valuable over time, not less.

data_unused.headline: Miners use less than 1% of the data their equipment produces
data_unused.figure: miners use less than 1 percent of the information collected from their equipment
data_unused.aside: average overall equipment effectiveness of 27 percent for underground mining and 39 percent for open-pit, against 88 percent for upstream oil and gas
data_unused.title: How digital innovation can improve mining productivity
data_unused.scope: 2015 vintage; the OEE contrast is the durable part of the finding. Kept because it is the clearest published statement of the specific condition this engagement addresses: the telemetry is already being collected.

ai_value_gap.headline: 60% of companies get hardly any material value from AI
ai_value_gap.figure: 5% of firms worldwide are in this camp, while 35% are scaling AI... But 60% companies are reaping hardly any material value
ai_value_gap.title: The Widening AI Value Gap
ai_value_gap.scope: Cross-industry, not mining. Quoted verbatim including the publisher's own grammatical slip. Printed as the counterweight to every uplift figure on these screens.

quartile_gap.headline: Top-quartile sites run 6% higher truck availability than average
quartile_gap.figure: companies with scores in the top quartile of the OHI had truck availability that was 8 percent higher than companies in the bottom quartile, and 6 percent higher than average OHI performers
quartile_gap.aside: that 8 percent difference could translate into a production increase of around 5 percent, or a decrease in operations costs of about 2 percent
quartile_gap.title: The missing link in mining-company productivity: People
quartile_gap.scope: Cross-mine benchmark linking Organizational Health Index quartile to physical equipment performance. The gap is attributed to operational discipline and accountability, not to technology.

discipline_gap.headline: 16% higher effective equipment use, on discipline alone
discipline_gap.figure: top quartile results in 'Accountability' and 'Operational discipline' achieved 16 percent higher UEE than those in the bottom quartile
discipline_gap.title: The missing link in mining-company productivity: People
discipline_gap.scope: Utilisation of Equipment Effectiveness, quartile to quartile. Named here because consistency of practice, not new plant, is what moves it.

guidance_miss.headline: Producers came in 2.4% under their own 12-month forecast
guidance_miss.figure: In the past five years, top mining companies have missed production targets, meaning they have missed out on $64 billion in revenue and have typically performed 2.4% worse than forecasted by themselves 12 months earlier. In the same five-year period, 60% of mines reported results at or below the lower half of the guidance range.
guidance_miss.aside: the missed production volumes amount to 213 million tons
guidance_miss.title: The mining industry's $64 billion blind spot
guidance_miss.scope: Public production announcements from major producers, 2020-2024. This is guidance against actual, NOT block model against mill reconciliation — the two are different measurements and the screen must not conflate them. The measure is asymmetric by construction: it counts shortfalls and excludes overproduction.

uplift.metric: production lost against the operator's own guidance

mature_ai_uplift.headline: 2–5% throughput, 2–4pp margin, from mature applications
mature_ai_uplift.figure: Sites report throughput improvements of 2% to 5%, margin improvements of 2 to 4 percentage points, and reductions in unplanned downtime
mature_ai_uplift.title: The AI-Powered Mining and Metals Company
mature_ai_uplift.scope: "Mature applications" in the publisher's own words — traditional machine learning, setpoint optimisation, digital twins, computer-vision safety. This is the conservative end of the published range and the most recent of the throughput figures, which is why it anchors the low side.

throughput_100_assets.headline: 8–10% throughput, recovery up 1–3 percentage points
throughput_100_assets.figure: potential to achieve 8 to 10 percent in throughput improvement as well as an uptick of one to three percentage points in recovery
throughput_100_assets.aside: alongside 8 to 10 percent throughput improvement, observed across more than 100 assets across industries and commodities globally
throughput_100_assets.title: Advancing metals and mining in Southeast Asia with digital and analytics
throughput_100_assets.scope: Observed across a stated base of 100+ assets, which makes this the best evidenced of the throughput figures and the reason it sets the middle of the range rather than the top.

concentrator_uplift.headline: 10–15% throughput, 2–4pp recovery at one concentrator
concentrator_uplift.figure: the plant improved throughput by a range of 10 to 15 percent, and copper recovery in a range of two to four percentage points
concentrator_uplift.title: OptimusAI
concentrator_uplift.scope: A single concentrator, on the publisher's own capability page. It is the top of the published range and it is not an industry benchmark — one plant is one plant. Printed because it bounds the range honestly at both ends, and labelled as a single site wherever it appears. The page carries no publication date; the year below records when it was read, and is not a claim about when the work was done.

haulage_ahs.headline: 20% productivity improvement from autonomous haulage
haulage_ahs.figure: miners using autonomous haulage technology have reported a 20 percent improvement in productivity
haulage_ahs.title: Behind the mining productivity upswing: Technology-enabled transformation
haulage_ahs.scope: Reported by Western Australian operators running autonomous haulage fleets. It is a fleet-automation figure, not a decision-support one — quoted as the ceiling of what fleet productivity work has returned, not as what this estate claims.

unit_cost_reduction.headline: Outperformers cut unit costs 3–6% a year, compounding
unit_cost_reduction.figure: reduced unit costs by an average compound annual rate of 3 to 6 percent
unit_cost_reduction.title: Mining for operational excellence
unit_cost_reduction.scope: Operational-excellence outperformers against their own baseline, compound annual. Cost per unit of output, which spans procurement, consumables and maintenance rather than any single line.

procurement.headline: Procurement productivity up to 50%
procurement.figure: improved their procurement productivity by up to 50%
procurement.title: Racing Toward a Digital Future in Metals and Mining
procurement.scope: Upper end of a range observed among digitally mature metals and mining companies; quoted as a ceiling, not a typical result. The same publication's digital-maturity finding has since been revised by BCG and is no longer printed — see `superseded`.

uplift.metric: higher procurement productivity, at the ceiling

opex_production_safety.headline: 1–16% production uplift, 5–23% fewer safety incidents
opex_production_safety.figure: with uplifts in production ranging from 1 to 16 percent and a reduction of safety incidents by 5 to 23 percent per annum
opex_production_safety.aside: a near-eradication of risk, with incidents per million hours reducing by half
opex_production_safety.title: How mining companies reach the operational excellence gold standard
opex_production_safety.scope: Self-selected operators who adopted an operational-excellence programme built on Shingo principles. The width of the production range is the finding: the same discipline returns 1 percent at one site and 16 at another. The aside is a single unnamed miner, not the cohort.

icmm_safety.headline: 39 fatalities across ICMM's 26 members in 2025
icmm_safety.figure: ICMM's 26 members recorded 39 fatalities in 2025. This compares to 43 fatalities in 2024, 35 in 2023, 33 in 2022, and 45 in 2021.
icmm_safety.aside: Our members reported 6,183 total recordable injuries (TRIs) in 2025; this is the lowest number recorded since ICMM began collecting member safety performance data in 2008.
icmm_safety.title: Safety Performance: Benchmarking progress of ICMM company members in 2025
icmm_safety.scope: 26 member companies, roughly a third of the industry and among its best operators, so this is a floor rather than an average. The fatality count has not trended down over five years while recordable injuries have, which is the point: severity and frequency are not the same problem. The publisher's page also states a percentage against a different hazard set and denominator; only the counts above are printed.

icmm_hazards.headline: Four hazards account for 87% of fatalities
icmm_hazards.figure: 'Fall of ground' and 'mobile equipment' were the most frequently recorded hazards in 2025, with 10 fatalities attributed to each.
icmm_hazards.aside: Together, these four hazards were responsible for 34 fatalities, representing 87% of the total recorded in 2025
icmm_hazards.title: Safety Performance: Benchmarking progress of ICMM company members in 2025
icmm_hazards.scope: Concentration, not rate. Named here because a concentrated hazard profile is what makes continuous monitoring worth doing at all: four categories, not a diffuse long tail.

excluded.figure: 20% EBITDA uplift / $3 return per $1 spent on AI
excluded.reason: Appears only in press coverage of remarks, with no named publication. Also not mining-specific. Note that McKinsey's own OptimusAI page publishes 4-5% EBITDA uplift for processing-plant productivity, which is an order of magnitude below the circulating figure.

excluded.figure: 42% EBITDA increase over a three-year programme
excluded.attributed_to: Boston Consulting Group, The Mining Productivity Imperative
excluded.reason: Search snippet only. Re-checked 2026-08-13 against BCG's January 2026 flagship mining publication; the figure does not appear there either.

excluded.figure: $370 billion per year / 17 percent of the cost base
excluded.attributed_to: McKinsey, Performing under pressure: Implementing innovation in mining
excluded.reason: WITHDRAWN BY PUBLISHER. The article page now reads "The article you are looking for is being revised and will be republished in due course." The companion claim that mining productivity has decreased by half comes from the same withdrawn piece. Not citable in any form until republished.

excluded.figure: $425bn of value to the mining and metals industry over ten years
excluded.attributed_to: World Economic Forum, Digital Transformation Initiative, 2017
excluded.reason: Rejected twice. The WEF-hosted PDF 302-redirects to a landing page and the live 2017 publication page links only to a cross-industry summary. The full text is reachable only through third-party mirrors.

excluded.figure: 90% reduction in haulage cost per tonne / 82.5% reduction in human workload
excluded.attributed_to: World Economic Forum, Global Lighthouse / MINDS cohort, 2026
excluded.reason: Single self-reported vendor deployment. Lighthouse figures are operator-supplied and survivorship-biased by the award's own design — a cohort of sites selected for having succeeded. The 2025 cohort's "53% boost in labour productivity" spans all sectors, not mining.

excluded.figure: Any Deloitte figure from Tracking the Trends
excluded.reason: The Tracking the Trends PDFs are primary sources but exceed the 10MB fetch limit and could not be read. Deloitte Insights HTML articles ARE reachable — the 2026 outlook grade-decline figure above was read that way. Route future Deloitte work through Insights HTML, not the flagship PDFs.

excluded.figure: 15% to 30% cost reduction / 10% to 25% EBITDA uplift
excluded.reason: bain.com returns HTTP 403 behind Cloudflare to both automated fetch and a real browser session. No Bain figure has ever been confirmed.
Not present on the current product page, which publishes only a 15-25% site cost reduction. The snippet reflects a superseded version of the page.

excluded.figure: 85,000 metric tons of ore per day; recovery rose by one percentage point
excluded.reason: Snippet-level; the specific page carrying it was not reached. The Freeport case study that WAS read publishes 5-10% production uplift, but its $350M-$500M EBITDA and 200M lb figures are projections from scaling the approach across the portfolio, not measured single-site results.

excluded.figure: Gen AI cut fleet fuel consumption by up to 10 percent
excluded.reason: The 10 percent figure IS in the primary source, but attributed there to "Traditional AI models" — not generative AI. The circulating snippet misattributes it. Rejected as quoted; the correctly attributed version was not adopted because fuel consumption is not a mechanism any agent in this estate addresses.

excluded.figure: Zhengzhou Coal Mining Machinery Group productivity figures
excluded.reason: A trap. The case carries a Mining & Metals tag and strong numbers, but the site is a hydraulic-support manufacturing plant, not a mine. Nothing in it transfers to an operating pit or concentrator.
Figures are gated behind a member portal.

CSIRO describes ore loss and dilution qualitatively. No published figure to quote. Searched specifically because pool B2 has no external benchmark; none was found anywhere, which is itself reported on screen.

superseded.figure: Mining is 30–40% less digitally mature than comparable industries
superseded.reason: BCG's January 2026 flagship revises its own position: mining "has gone from near the bottom to the middle of the pack, according to BCG's Build for the Future research." Printing the 2021 gap alongside the 2026 publication would misrepresent the publisher.

superseded.figure: Mining productivity declined 3.5 percent per year / 28 percent less efficient
superseded.reason: McKinsey's 2022 operational-excellence work restates the same period differently — "the ten largest companies in the mining industry have seen only marginal growth of around 1 percent" against manufacturing at 15 and business services at 25 percent over 25 years. Marginal growth and a 28 percent decline cannot both be printed. Replaced by the PwC 2026 labour productivity figure, which is current and unambiguous.

Superseded within the throughput range by three more recent and better scoped sources: BCG 2026 at 2-5%, McKinsey 2023 at 8-10% across 100+ assets, and McKinsey's OptimusAI concentrator at 10-15%. The 2018 figure's "5 to 10 percent productivity, roughly equivalent to opening a new mine without the capital cost" aside was rhetorically useful and is deliberately not carried forward — it is the kind of line that makes a deck read as a brochure.

superseded.figure: Only ~5% of companies get a tenth of their EBIT from gen AI
superseded.reason: Replaced by BCG's "60% companies are reaping hardly any material value", which measures the same scepticism from the majority side rather than the exceptional side and is the more recent survey. Both are cross-industry; printing two versions of one finding pads the evidence base.
